title: Declining discount rates

definition.text: Declining discount rates start relatively high for the near future and fall over time, to reflect long-term uncertainty and ethical concerns.

facts.text: Recent literature on the social cost of carbon supports declining rather than constant discount rates.
One climate model in the Stern Review debate used a 3% social discount rate that slowly declines to 1% over 300 years.
Over long periods, people's stated time preferences become extremely hyperbolic.

notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own.

title: Quasi-option value

definition.text: Quasi-option value is the extra value of keeping future choices open when a decision's consequences may be irreversible and uncertain.

facts.text: Arrow and Fischer (1974) and Epstein (1980) showed that possible irreversible consequences create a quasi-option effect that leads even a risk-neutral society to favour flexible decisions.
It grew out of option value, which depends on uncertain future need for an asset, irreversibility or high replacement cost if it is lost, and the asset not being storable.
In climate policy, the possible irreversibility of damage to biomes and ecosystems is weighed against the irreversibility of investing in emission cuts.
Economists have analysed the precautionary principle as the interaction of irreversibility and uncertainty.

notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own; also called the irreversibility effect.
